research_question: When two same-direction quarter-hour common-flow impulses fail to sustain price discovery, does majority reacceptance of the second impulse origin create a frequent and cost-positive market-wide failed-auction reversal?

evidence_basis.v9: Direct same-direction follower retests produced 126 protected QH trades, 42 wins and 84 losses after exact removal of six unprotected child-stop-rejection episodes.
evidence_basis.v10: Persistent same-direction initiatives produced 99 QHI fills, 15 wins and 84 losses. Of 1,012 completed initiative states, 611 terminated by majority origin reacceptance with a median lifetime of 15 minutes and 401 terminated by an opposite common-flow event with a median lifetime of 30 minutes.
evidence_basis.interpretation: The recurring event is real and frequent, but continuation is not the default state. Majority reacceptance is an observable failed-auction transition rather than a loss-derived magnitude threshold.

hypothesis.context: At least three of BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP complete the first five minutes of a UTC quarter-hour with the same directional displacement and same-signed taker flow.
hypothesis.attempted_initiative: A second distinct common-flow event in the same direction before any opposite event establishes a two-impulse market-wide price-discovery attempt. No trade is placed yet.
hypothesis.failure_transition: At a completed five-minute boundary, a majority of the second event's accepted markets close back through their own second-event origins. This observable reacceptance invalidates the attempted initiative.
hypothesis.tradable_markets: Only markets accepted in both the first and second events and individually reaccepted through the second origin may propose a reversal. Simultaneous proposals compete through the unchanged global one-slot arbitration.
hypothesis.entry: Post-only limit at the second event origin, which becomes resistance after a failed long initiative and support after a failed short initiative.
hypothesis.invalidation: Beyond the second event extreme plus the inherited ATR buffer. Re-entering the failed impulse range beyond its extreme invalidates the reversal leg.
hypothesis.target: The first event origin in the opposite direction. This is the beginning of the failed two-impulse campaign and belongs to the same causal auction sequence.
hypothesis.expiry: The inherited structural retrace expiry of twelve completed five-minute bars. A later unfilled retest is no longer the same failed-auction entry.
hypothesis.cost_contract: Entry and target are maker assumptions, stop is taker, and plans below the inherited 1.25 after-cost structural R floor are rejected before order submission.
hypothesis.execution_safety: Any denied or rejected child protection after a parent fill triggers immediate cancel-and-flatten. The run still fails its safety audit.
hypothesis.independence: One plan per market per distinct two-event failure identity. Repeated prints inside the same failure do not create new scenario IDs.

selection.method: The same six already-exposed V9/V10 diagnostic weeks are reused only for mechanism development. They can reject or redesign V11 but can never support a success claim.

claim_rules: E01-E06 are exposed development periods and cannot support a success claim.
V11 is a distinct failed-auction scenario family; it does not select winning V10 trades or tune magnitude thresholds.
A positive result must advance unchanged to a broader exposed screen, source freeze and untouched continuous validation.
